# One row per mirrored file: vault-relative path <TAB> class <TAB> why it is doctrine.
# tools/corpus-sync.py reads this file and nothing else to decide what to mirror.
# Adding doctrine to the corpus = adding a row. Removing one = deleting the row
# (then --sync --prune). The Drive copy stays canonical either way.
# THE TEST APPLIED (ORDER 30's criterion, stated so the next editor applies the same one):
#   IN  — the file teaches how the work is done or what is true about the domain,
#         and it changes only when a human decides to change it.
#   OUT — records, rosters, registries, ledgers, queues, briefs, dated research
#         snapshots, generated exports, indexes/pointers, and session state.
#   OUT — anything whose content is instructions for running a pipeline that the
#         record layer is actively rewriting (the SOP class). Those are the
#         open QUESTIONS in ORDER 30's log, deliberately unmirrored in phase 1.
